chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Hasan the first (peace be upon him)
Regarding the one struck by lightning and the drowned: He (peace be upon him) said: They are awaited for three days, unless their state changes before that.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for determining death in cases of lightning strike or drowning?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'tadarruj al-mawt' (gradual death), establishing a three-day observation period for those struck by lightning or drowned to determine if death is final. Scholars note this ruling balances the presumption of life with practical signs of decay, ensuring that premature burial does not occur if there is still a possibility of revival. It reflects the Imams' emphasis on careful verification in legal matters where the boundary between life and death is ambiguous.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup>
regarding the one struck by lightning and the drowned. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They would be awaited with for three days except if (their state) were to alter before that’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam

who has said the following: “About people found dead because of a sudden shock or drowned, abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said to wait three days unless a change in their condition takes place earlier.’”
